question: A payments company is designing its audit logging architecture on Google Cloud before a regulatory examination. The regulator expects complete audit trails of both configuration changes and data access, evidence that logs cannot be tampered with by the teams being audited, and assurance that new projects are covered automatically. Which three design decisions should you make? (Choose three.)

Create an organization-level aggregated sink that routes audit logs to a destination in a dedicated logging project that application teams cannot access.
Grant the roles/logging.admin role to all project owners so they can adjust retention as needed.
Apply a locked retention policy on the destination Cloud Storage bucket, or lock the destination log bucket, so retained logs cannot be deleted or shortened before the retention period ends.
Rely on the _Required bucket for all audit evidence because it already stores every audit log type for 400 days.
explanation: Completeness requires enabling Data Access logs organization-wide since they are off by default; independence from the audited teams requires routing logs through an organization-level aggregated sink into a separate project they cannot modify; and tamper evidence requires locking the destination's retention so no one can delete logs early. Option B keeps logs where the audited teams have control and only 30 days of retention. Option D hands audited teams the ability to change retention, undermining integrity. Option F is wrong because _Required stores only Admin Activity, System Event and Access Transparency logs, not Data Access logs, and 400 days may not meet regulatory retention.
hint: Core Rule (Audit logging design): Completeness requires enabling Data Access logs organization-wide since they are off by default; independence from the audited teams requires routing logs through an organization-level aggregated sink into a separate project they cannot modify; and tamper evidence requires locking the destination's retention so no one can delete logs early.

question: A security engineer created an organization-level aggregated sink to route audit logs to a BigQuery dataset in a central security project.
